lines.2: 「...Cut it out. People will get the wrong idea.」
lines.3: 「You don't appreciate my improvised young-wife act? I thought married women were your thing.」
lines.5: 「So you went out blowing money again? You don't even have a steady part-time job. How the hell do you afford it?」
lines.6: 「That intensive spring-break gig is still paying off.」
lines.8: 「A wild bear was once again lured into a private residence by food, but was safely returned to the mountains.」
lines.10: 「All right, kid. Dinner's ready. Beef short ribs piled high with vegetables, green-onion miso soup, and wood ear and butterbur with sesame mayonnaise.」
lines.11: Subaru briskly arranged everything on the table.
lines.12: 「Oh, how can I ever repay you?」
lines.13: 「Save it and eat before it gets cold.」
lines.18: Subaru, despite appearances, was a master chef.
lines.19: He was the one who always made my dinner.
lines.20: ...No, we weren't in that kind of relationship, okay?
lines.21: Subaru's parents had a falling-out and his mother left home, so he tried to spend as little time as possible in the house with his father. (His place was three doors down.)
lines.22: His father had once been considered a tremendously promising track athlete, but things happened, his career collapsed, and he turned to booze and women.
lines.23: So in a sense, Subaru said this was where he belonged.
lines.24: I provided the kitchen, rice, seasonings, and a place to eat.
lines.25: Subaru bought the ingredients, cooked them here, and ate. (And made enough for me while he was at it.)
lines.26: It was a simple give-and-take arrangement.
lines.27: Not every day, but we did this three or four nights a week.
lines.28: I told my parents overseas that I cooked for myself properly.
lines.29: It wasn't technically a lie, so I figured it was fine.
lines.30: 「This would be perfect if only you were a cute girl.」
lines.31: 「Don't start talking like Fukahire, running away from reality.」
lines.33: 「Well, reality is what it is, Tsushima.」
